findings.location: walker-playback.md section 4 (final paragraph) and FR-WP1 AC3
findings.problem: Describes the HistorySource binding as a FileRef that has versions()/reconstruct(version) methods. The real FR-K1 trait places versions(&self, &FileRef) and reconstruct(&self, &FileRef, &VersionId) on HistorySource, not on FileRef, and uses walker-side VersionId rather than walrus_fmt::Version.
findings.fix: Reword to the trait's real shape: the group is exposed through HistorySource; source.versions(&group_ref) and source.reconstruct(&group_ref, VersionId::Index(k)) return the document versions and office bytes (WalrusSource maps VersionId to walrus_fmt::Version and calls extract_office).

findings.problem: States the office view calls archive.extract_office directly, while also routing the group through the HistorySource seam. Both end at extract_office so there is no behavioural conflict, but two reconstruction paths are described; a direct archive.extract_office call from the view would reintroduce the walrus_fmt dependency FR-K1/FR-K8 isolate.
findings.fix: Make the seam the single normative path: the view obtains bytes via HistorySource::reconstruct(&group_ref, VersionId::Index(player.index())); WalrusSource is the only place that calls archive.extract_office.

findings.problem: Contrasts against player.current_bytes() reconstructing 'a single tracked file'. Accurate for today's single-file player.rs, but in the multi-file HistorySource world (FR-K2/FR-K8) reconstruction already goes through the seam, so the contrast point is slightly out of date.
findings.fix: Contrast against the seam's reconstruct rather than the legacy Player::current_bytes, consistent with finding 2.
